slides.text:
A Go function can return several values: list the types in parentheses. The caller takes all of them in one `:=`, or discards one with `_`.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.

The common use is a result plus an `error`. By convention the error comes last, and `nil` means it worked. The caller checks it right away.

`error` and `errors.New` are used as they come here. They are taught in depth in the error handling course.
Results can have names. They start at their zero value, and a bare `return` sends them back.

chunks.guide: The error is the last result. `nil` says nothing went wrong.
On failure return a zero value and an error.

Takes two strings and returns one.
`swap` returns two values and `join` takes exactly two: pass the call straight in.

notes.text: Named results are variables that start at 0.
